clue.text: Damages route into island

indicators.note: into says the road piece is placed inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island
ST is the abbreviation for street, a route

explanation.surface: Legal compensation is claimed for a road built across an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' is the container signal; 'Damages' looks like a verb in the surface but is the plural noun for money awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Damages, as losses or expenses suffered, are costs.

clue.text: Be persuaded to pay a visit

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to be won over to a view and to drop in on someone.

clue.text: One recruited to join up

indicators.note: recruited to says the one is enlisted into the joining word

parts.note: to solder is to join metal pieces
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is enlisted to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recruited to' puts I inside SOLDER; the whole clue also describes someone who has enlisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A recruit who joins up is a member of an army.

clue.text: Hospital bed's set up to accommodate one patient

indicators.note: to accommodate says the reversed beds take in the next piece
set up in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: cots are beds, as in a hospital
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A hospital bed is assembled to take one sick person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' reverses COTS to STOC; 'to accommodate' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoic as an adjective means enduring hardship without complaint.

clue.text: U for Uccello, perhaps?

parts.note: U is the top letter of Uccello, a Renaissance painter or drawer; U is also the shorthand for upper-class, i.e. of the finest sort

explanation.surface: An alphabet book entry: U is for Uccello.
explanation.walkthrough: Paolo Uccello was an Italian painter, a drawer; U stands at his top. 'U' also means upper-class in British usage, and the phrase means first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means of the highest social class or quality, which is what U (upper-class) signified.

clue.text: The list arranged in order

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the words before it are put in another sequence

explanation.surface: A list sorted into sequence.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of the Thistle is Scotland's senior order of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thistle is a Scottish order of knighthood.

clue.text: Display part of book, a collection of Christian writings

parts.note: a page is part of a book
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: Showing a page of a religious anthology.
explanation.definitionFit: A pageant is a spectacular show or procession.

clue.text: Regarding the sweet I had to reject

parts.note: re means about or regarding
pud is British slang for pudding, a dessert
had a meal means ate

explanation.surface: Someone had to turn down a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to refuse to accept or disown.

clue.text: Acquire a few points full of charm

parts.note: to win is to acquire
some means a few, as in winning a few of the points

explanation.surface: Scoring a few points in a charming way.
explanation.definitionFit: Winsome means engaging and attractive.

clue.text: The laws of football, as played in Perth

definitions.meaning: Australian ... football, the game played in Perth, Western Australia

explanation.definitionFit: Regulations are this word, and Aussie Rules is the code of football dominant in Perth.

clue.text: Some caramel, low in glucose, becoming sweeter

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diet note: a little caramel, kept low in glucose, still tastes sweeter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mellowing means growing softer and richer in flavour, so becoming sweeter.

clue.text: Glass left on board

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: Someone has left a glass sitting on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel is a flat board, as in wooden panelling.

clue.text: Grandad's actions ruined bucket

indicators.note: ruined says the letters of the words before it are wrecked and rebuilt

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: An old man's behaviour has wrecked a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bucket' is the verb, as in 'it's bucketing down'; the phrase is the idiom for very heavy rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To bucket is to pour with rain, and the idiom describes a downpour.

clue.text: Heighten universal acclaim

parts.note: U is the film classification for universal
praise is acclaim

explanation.surface: An instruction to increase acclaim everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To upraise is an old word for to raise up or elevate.

clue.text: Thereby a post office is rebuilt without bits of iron

indicators.note: is rebuilt says the letters of the phrase are put together anew

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, its two letters

explanation.surface: A post office is rebuilt without iron girders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes F and E from the letters of A POST OFFICE before the rest are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, hence thereby.

clue.text: Hear about old disaster

indicators.note: about says the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case
aged means old

explanation.surface: Listen to the story of an old calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is the container signal; 'Hear' is used in the courtroom sense of judging a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a terrible event, a catastrophe.

clue.text: Why, say, church festival has lost original character in recent past

parts.note: the letter Y sounds like why

indicators.note: has lost says a letter is dropped from what comes before

parts.note: Easter Day is the church festival
A, the first letter of the alphabet, is the original character

explanation.surface: An Easter festival has lost its old character lately.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A out of Y + EASTER DAY leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The recent past is the day before today, or time gone by not long ago.

clue.text: Moves out of office and gives evidence

definitions.meaning: testifies under oath, as a witness does

explanation.definitionFit: To depose is both to oust a ruler and to make a sworn statement.

clue.text: Cry over error in financial record

indicators.note: over in a down clue says the word is turned upside down

parts.note: to yap is to cry like a small dog
a slip is a mistake

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a mistake in their accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A payslip is a note recording an employee's wages and deductions.

clue.text: An essential when climbing fruit tree

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue says the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: an gives A
a must is an essential
as means when

explanation.surface: Something essential when scaling a fruit tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A + MUST + AS reads upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The satsuma is a citrus tree bearing small mandarin-like fruit.

clue.text: Biological collection that's kept in glasses

indicators.note: kept in says the second piece is held inside the first

parts.note: specs is short for spectacles, glasses
IE is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A biologist's collection stored in spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept in' is the container signal; 'that's' stands for 'that is', the Latin id est.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a group of related organisms in biological classification.

clue.text: Excessively high, extremely large tower

parts.note: steep prices are excessively high

indicators.note: extremely says take the extreme, outermost letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A huge tower of excessive height.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped with a spire.

clue.text: Minor turning up in pub, pulled inside

indicators.note: in says the reversed piece sits inside the pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue says the word is read upwards

parts.note: a ward is a minor under a guardian

explanation.surface: An underage drinker turns up in a pub and is dragged inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' gives DRAW from the minor piece, and 'in' places that inside the pub word.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn breath is breath pulled in.

clue.text: Hammerhead may suddenly become ill-tempered

definitions.meaning: the head of a hammer may literally come loose from its shaft

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose one's temper abruptly; a loose hammerhead literally does the same.

clue.text: River to the South-East? That's not true

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
SE is the abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A dispute about whether a river flows to the south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is wrong or incorrect.

clue.text: Bolt from school, having lost head

indicators.note: having lost head says the first letter is taken off

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: A pupil runs off from school after losing their head.
explanation.walkthrough: HARROW is a well-known English boarding school; a bolt is a crossbow arrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolt is a short heavy projectile shot from a crossbow.

clue.text: Put back ring around one tree

indicators.note: put back says the whole assembly is read in reverse
around says the ring piece encloses the next

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to replace a ring around a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts I inside CALL to give CALIL; 'Put back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering shrub or small tree.

clue.text: Foreman, perhaps, in control

definitions.meaning: a foreman is a senior hand, a worker placed above others

explanation.definitionFit: Having the advantage over someone means having control; a foreman is a hand set above the rest.

clue.text: Page one is, unusually, showing intelligence

indicators.note: unusually says these words are set out in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A front page is showing unusual cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of spying and secret information-gathering.

clue.text: Tempestuous chicken

definitions.meaning: British slang for frightened or nervous

explanation.definitionFit: Stormy weather is blustery; in British slang being scared is being nervy.
